summary: Registers a URN namespace identifier for the Foundation for Intelligent Physical Agents (FIPA). It is used to identify standard components that FIPA publishes in the area of agent technology. This is a registration document for the namespace, not a protocol specification.

eli5.summary: Robots and software helpers need a common list of names for their parts. This document gives one group a special name prefix, so everyone can write down the same part names and mean the same thing.

questions: what is the fipa urn namespace
how do you create a urn namespace
subtitle: A standardized naming system for agent technology components.

tldr.problem: The Foundation for Intelligent Physical Agents (FIPA) needed a way to create and manage globally unique, persistent identifiers for its technical specifications and standards related to agent technology.
tldr.mechanism: This RFC registers a URN (Uniform Resource Name) namespace with the identifier 'fipa', allowing FIPA to assign structured names like urn:fipa:language:acl or urn:fipa:ontology:management to its published components.
tldr.outcome: FIPA gained an official, standards-track namespace managed by its Architecture Board, enabling unambiguous identification of agent specifications across different platforms and vendors.

today: RFC 3616 is an Informational RFC that successfully registered the 'fipa' URN namespace with IANA. FIPA continues to manage this namespace through its Architecture Board, using it to identify published specifications in agent technology.

sections.title: Foundation for Intelligent Physical Agents
sections.content:
The Foundation for Intelligent Physical Agents (FIPA) is an international non-profit organization established in 1996 that brings together companies and organizations to develop specifications for intelligent agents. Its core mission is to facilitate interoperability among agents and agent-based systems across multiple vendors' platforms. FIPA publishes technical specifications, schemas, diagrams and documentation related to agent technology.

FIPA needed a way to create globally unique, persistent identifiers for its published resources that are independent of location and managed by FIPA itself to ensure integrity and correctness.
sections.eli5: A group of companies works together to create standards for robot-like computer programs. They needed official names for all the parts of those standards.

sections.title: URN Namespace Basics
sections.content:
A Uniform Resource Name (URN) is a persistent, location-independent identifier. A URN namespace is a managed collection of unique identifiers following a specific structure. FIPA registered the namespace identifier 'fipa', allowing it to assign URNs with a hierarchical structure using colons as separators.

The structure follows the pattern urn:fipa:subspace-id1:subspace-id2:..., where each subspace-id is an ASCII string without colons. This allows FIPA to organize identifiers logically by standardization area, technical committee, or other schemes.
sections.eli5: A URN is like a permanent mailing address for a specification that never changes no matter where it is stored. FIPA's namespace lets them create addresses that start with 'urn:fipa:' followed by category names.

sections.title: FIPA's Namespace Structure
sections.content:
FIPA designed its namespace to support multiple organizational schemes. Examples include organizing by standardization area (such as urn:fipa:language:acl for the Agent Communication Language or urn:fipa:ontology:management for management ontologies), or by technical committee (such as urn:fipa:architecture:example:directory).

The namespace structure reflects the logical organization of FIPA specifications without reference to domain names or other location-based elements. The FIPA Architecture Board (FAB) manages the assignment of all URNs, ensuring uniqueness and correctness. FIPA commits to maintaining the availability and persistence of all identified resources.
sections.eli5: FIPA groups its standards by topic, like 'language' for how agents talk, or 'ontology' for shared vocabularies. Everything gets a permanent name that follows the same pattern.

sections.title: Benefits for Developers and Users
sections.content:
Standardized URNs benefit multiple stakeholders. The FIPA standards process gains unique labels for specification components, making them easier to reference and version. Developers implementing FIPA-based systems can unambiguously identify which specifications are in use, allowing software to flexibly distinguish between different technologies.

Network users benefit from improved integrity and clarity of interactions in systems using FIPA technology. They can precisely identify technology requirements when interacting with any given software system. FIPA maintains published lists of assigned identifiers on its website for resolution and discovery.
sections.eli5: When a programmer writes software using FIPA standards, they can tell the computer 'use this specification' by its URN. Then any other program knows exactly which standard to follow.

sections.title: Security and Management
sections.content:
The FIPA URN namespace shares the general security considerations outlined in RFC 3406, which covers URN namespace definition mechanisms. Since URNs are persistent identifiers and not cryptographically bound, security depends on operational practices and the trusted management of the namespace.

FIPA mitigates risks through its Architecture Board's centralized management of identifier assignment and FIPA's commitment to maintaining the persistence and availability of resources identified by URNs. The namespace assignment process is open to FIPA members following the established standards process.
sections.eli5: Since anyone could theoretically try to use a fake FIPA name, the real FIPA group keeps a list of official names on their website so people can verify which ones are real.

references.text: Daigle, L., van Gulik, D., Iannella, R. and P. Faltstrom, "Uniform Resource Names (URN) Namespace Definition Mechanisms", BCP 66, RFC 3406, October 2002.
